# Scenario

The Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) have a long-term
inshore marine water quality monitoring program in which water samples
are collected and analysed from sites (reef.alias) across the GBR numerous times
per year.  The focus of this program is to report long-term condition and change
in water quality parameters.

Although we do have latitude and longitudes, the nature of the spatial design
predominantly reflects a series of transects that start near the mouth of a
major river and extend northwards, yet mainly within the open coastal zone.  As
a result, this design is not well suited to any specific spatial analyses (since
they are mainly one dimensional).

![AIMS water quality monitoring](../resources/AIMS_wq.jpg){#fig-aims width="600" height="325"}

\...     \...      \...       \...          \...   \...      \...   \...      \...

: Format of aims.wq.csv data file {#tbl-aims .table-condensed}

--------------     ---------------------------------------------------------------------
**LATITUDE**       - Latitudinal coordinate
**LONGITUDE**      - Longitudinal coordinate
**reef.alias**     - Internal AIMS reef name
**Water_Samples**  - Categorical label of who collected the data
**Region**         - The MMP region
**Subregion**      - The MMP subregion
**Season**         - A categorical listing of Wet or Dry
**waterYear**      - The water year (1st Oct - 30 Sept) to which the data are attached
**Date**           - The date the sample was collected
**Mnth**           - The month the sample was collected
**NOx**            - Nitrite and Nitrate
--------------     ---------------------------------------------------------------------

: Description of the variables in the aims data file {#tbl-aims1 .table-condensed}

# Read in the data

```{r}
#| label: readData
#| cache: false
wq <- read_csv("../data/aims_wq.csv", trim_ws = TRUE)
```

<!-- START_PRIVATE-->
We will start by defining each of the categorical variables as factors.  We will
also define the random effect (reef.alias) as a factor.

```{r}
#| label: prepareData
#| cache: false
wq <- wq |>
    mutate(
        Site = factor(Site),
        Region = factor(Region),
        Subregion = factor(Subregion),
        Season = factor(Season)
    )
```



<!-- END_PRIVATE-->

# Exploratory data analysis

Model formula:
$$
\begin{align}
y_i &\sim{} \mathcal{N}(\mu_i, \sigma^2)\\
\mu_i &=\beta_0 + f(Date_i) + f(Month_i)
\end{align}
$$

where $\beta_0$ is the y-intercept. $f(Date)$ and $f(Month)$ indicate the additive smoothing functions of the long-term temporal trends and the annual seasonal trends respectively.

<!-- START_PRIVATE-->
If we begin with a quck scatterplot of NOx agains Date..

```{r}
#| label: EDA1a
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 12
#| mhidden: true
#| eval: true
#| out-width: 800px
#| warning: false
#| message: false
wq |> ggplot(aes(y = NOx, x = Date)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ Region + Site, scales = "free_y") +
  geom_smooth()
```

```{r}
#| label: EDA1aa
#| mhidden: true
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
wq |> ggplot(aes(y = NOx)) +
    geom_boxplot()
```

We know that these NOx values have been measured over time from a number of
locations (reef.alias).  Therefore, it would be good to facet the scatterplot
conditional on the reef.alias.


```{r}
#| label: EDA1b
#| eval: true
#| mhidden: true
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 12
#| out-width: 800px
#| warning: false
#| message: false
ggplot(wq, aes(y = NOx, x = Date)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = Season)) +
    geom_smooth() +
    facet_wrap(~Region + Site, scales = 'free_y')
```

**Conclusions:**

- evidently, some locations (reef.alias) have longer time series than others
- the amount and variability of NOx also varies greatly between locations.
- the temporal trends are clearly not linear and possibly more complex than
  simple polynomials - it is likely that splines will be useful
- assumptions of normality are difficult to assess, however it would seem
  logical that the data will not follow a Gaussian distribution (since values
  less than 0 are not possible and it does appear that there is a relationship
  between mean and variance).
- although not immediately obvious from some of the trends, the values
  of NOx appear to be truncated at 0.01. Indeed the limit of detection
  is 0.01 and thus values are capped at this value.

```{r}
#| label: EDA1c
#| eval: true
#| mhidden: true
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 12
#| out-width: 800px
#| warning: false
#| message: false
ggplot(wq, aes(y=NOx, x=Date)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
    scale_y_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(trans=scales::pseudo_log_trans()) +
  facet_wrap(~Site,  scales='free_y')

```

**Conclusions:**

- although the loess smoothers are not particularly appropriate for non-Gaussian
  data, they nevertheless help us see that there are both similarities and
  differnces in the trends between locations.   Most of the locations that have
  a long time series show some sort of peak in NOx around about 2014


<!-- END_PRIVATE-->

# Data preparations

<!-- START_PRIVATE-->

Care must be taken when using dates in a model. This is because they
are stored either as number of seconds or the number of days that have
elapsed since a particular time. Typically, this means that they are
stored as very large numbers and any calculations that involve large
numbers can quickly become too large to handle efficiently. Hence, it
is often a good idea to convert dates/times into simpler numeric
representations. This can be performed with the `decimal_date()`
function within the `lubridate` package.

Although we generally want to scale any continuous predictors, it
appears that doing so with Date objects has downstream issues - the
models fit ok, but partial plots are displaced along the x-axis. So as
an alternative either dont scale, or do so with a routine that does
not automatically back-trasform (such as sjmisc::std or
sjmisc::center).

At this point, we can also add a predictor for month so as to
facilitate models that will detrend a temporal series into long-terms
and annual cycles. Furthermore, we will also establish a flag variable
to handle the truncated limit of detection values. This latter
variable will contain the string "left" for any value that is set to
the limit of detection/reporting and "none" for all other values.

```{r}
#| label: prepareData2
#| eval: true
#| mhidden: true
#| cache: false
wq <-
  wq |>
    mutate(dt_num = lubridate::decimal_date(Date)) |>
    mutate(Mnth = month(Date)) |>
    mutate(NOx_flag = ifelse(NOx == 0.01, "left", "none"))
```

<!-- END_PRIVATE-->

# Simple model (Double Island)


## Date (Dt_num) only


<!-- START_PRIVATE-->

::: {.panel-tabset}

When contemplating fitting a complex model, it is often good practice to build a
model up, starting with something relatively simple.  That way, if the model
fails or yeilds strange outcomes, it is easier to diagnose the issues.
In the spirit of this, we will begin by building up a temporal model for a
single reef (Pandora), before moving on to generalise across multiple reefs in a
mixed effects model.


### Exploratory data analysis


```{r}
#| label: model1a
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
#| mhidden: true
wq_sub <-
  wq |>
  filter(Site == "Double Island") |>
  droplevels()

wq_sub |>
  ggplot(aes(y = NOx, x = Date)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Season)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  scale_y_log10()

wq_sub |>
  filter(!is.na(NOx)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y=NOx, x=Date)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'gam', formula = y ~ s(x),
    method.args = list(family = Gamma(link = "log")))

wq_sub |>
  pull(NOx) |>
  summary()
```

**Conclusions:**

- of concern in the above figure is the set of DOC values of 0.01 at the start
  of the time series.  These values represent the limit of detection of the
  instrumentation used for measuring DOC at the time.  Any value measured at
  0.01 or less was just recorded as 0.01.
- ideally, such cases should be modelled as censored so as to acknowledge that
  they are at or below 0.01 and not exactly 0.01 (with no variation).
  Unfortunately, this is not available with the `mgcv` package (or any
  frequentist package for fitting GAM's that I am aware of).
- options for dealing with such circumstances very much depend on the
  reliability of these values.  If we believe that they are approximately
  representative, we might elect to keep them in an model as normal.  On the
  other hand, if the reliability of the measurements is questionable, we might
  elect to exclude these values.
- in the absence of any additional information about these observations, we will
  keep them in.



<!-- END_PRIVATE-->

### GAM

::::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Assessing default priors

```{r fitModel1a, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~
                s(dt_num), family = Gamma(link = "log"))
get_prior(wq_form, data =  wq_sub)

wq_brm <- brm(wq_form,
  data = wq_sub,
  prior = prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = 'b'),
  sample_prior = 'only',
  iter = 5000,
  warmup = 1000,
  chains = 3,
  thin = 5,
  seed = 123,
  backend = 'cmdstan',
  refresh = 0)
```

##### conditional_effects

```{r fitModel1d2, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE}
wq_brm |> conditional_effects() |>
  plot(points=TRUE) |>
  scale_y_log10()
```


#### Defining priors

The following link provides some guidance about defining priors.
[https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations]


::::: {.panel-tabset}

##### About priors

I will also overlay the raw data for comparison.

sds- wiggliness parameter

A model such as

`y ~ s(scale(x))`

represents the relationship between `x` and `y` using a set of spline
basis functions:

$$
f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{K} b_k B_k(x)
$$

In `brms`, the spline is separated into:

- b: unpenalised components, including the broad linear trend

- sds: the standard deviation of the penalised spline coefficients,
  controlling departures from that trend

Conceptually, the penalised coefficients have a prior of the form
$$
b_k^{\mathrm{smooth}} \sim \operatorname{Normal}(0,\sigma_s)
$$

where $\sigma_s$ is reported as `sds`.

###### Prior for b

The `b` prior controls the size of the broad change in the response
associated with the scaled predictor:

- a prior concentrated near zero favours a weak overall relationship
- a wider prior permits a stronger overall trend

Because `scale(x)` gives `x` mean zero and standard deviation one, `b`
can be interpreted approximately as the expected change in the linear
component of the response for a one-standard-deviation change in `x`.

Choose the prior using plausible effect sizes on the response scale. For example, if both `x` and `y` are standardised:

`prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b")` allows substantial positive or
negative effects while mildly discouraging extremely large
relationships.

If `y` is not standardised, select the prior scale in meaningful units of `y`. For example:

`prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b")`

says that changes of several response units per standard deviation of `x` are plausible.


###### Prior for sds

The `sds` parameter controls the complexity of the smooth:

- sds near zero favours an approximately linear relationship

- small sds permits gentle curvature

- large sds permits increasingly complex or wiggly relationships

Because sds must be positive, suitable weakly informative priors include half-normal, half-Student-ttt, and exponential distributions. For a standardised response, reasonable starting points are:

`prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "sds")`

or, more permissively:

`prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sds")`

`brms` automatically constrains `sds` to be positive, so these become half-normal or half-Student-t priors.

A useful interpretation is:

- The prior on `sds` expresses how strongly we expect the relationship to depart from a straight line.

Note, `sds` does not correspond to a particular distance along `x`. Its effect depends on the spline basis dimension and the observed predictor values. It should therefore be checked using prior predictive smooths.

Practical guidelines:

| Prior choice               | Interpretation                                        |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Narrower prior on b        | Stronger belief that the overall relationship is weak |
| Wider prior on b           | Allows a larger overall effect                        |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| sds concentrated near zero | Favours an approximately linear relationship          |
| Moderate prior on sds      | Allows smooth curvature                               |
| Very broad prior on sds    | Allows complex curves and may overfit sparse data     |


##### Sample prior only

```{r fitModel2aaa, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ s(scale(dt_num)), family = Gamma(link = "log"))

wq_sub |> summarise(
  median(log(NOx)),
  mad(log(NOx)),
  mad(log(NOx)) / mad(scale(dt_num))
)
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1),  class='Intercept') +
  prior(normal(0, 10), class='b') +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01),  class='shape') +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 10), class =  "sds")

wq_brm1 <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'only',
                 iter = 3000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 thin = 5,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 backend = 'cmdstanr',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 0)
```

```{r fitModel2b, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE}
wq_brm1 |> conditional_effects() |>  plot(points=TRUE)
wq_brm1 |> conditional_effects() |>  plot(points=TRUE) |>
  _[[1]] +
  scale_y_log10()

wq_brm1 |> conditional_effects() |>
  ## plot(points=TRUE, point_args = list(colour = "red", size = 4)) |>
  plot(points=TRUE) |>
  _[[1]] +
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_point(data = wq_sub, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(y = NOx, x = dt_num))
```

#### Model investigation


:::: {.panel-tabset}

##### Summary

```{r summariseModel1a, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
wq_brm2 |> summary()
```

- sds(sx_1) is the sd of the smooth weights (spline coefficients).

  - This determines the amount of ‘wiggliness’, and is analogous way
    to how the sd of group-level effects in a varying slopes and
    intercepts model determine the amount of variability among groups
    in slopes and intercepts.
  - However, the actual numeric value of the sds() is not very
    practically interpretable, because thinking about the variance of
    smooth weights for any given data and model seems abstract to me.
  - However, if the value is around zero, then this is like
    ‘complete-pooling’ of the basis functions, which means that there
    isn’t much added value of more than a single basis function.

- sx_1 is the unpenalized weight (ie coefficient) for one of the
  “natural” parameterized basis functions.
  - The rest of the basis functions are like varying effects.
  - Again, because the actual numeric value of sxs_1 is the value for
    the unpenalized coefficient for one of the basis functions.
  - his wouldn’t seem to have a lot of practically interpretable
    meaning just from viewing this number.

#### Find the peak

```{r}
#| label: simple Date peak
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
newdata <- with(wq_sub, data.frame(
  dt_num = seq(min(2010), max(2017), length = 1000)
))
wq_peak <-
    add_epred_draws(
        object = wq_brm2, newdata = newdata,
```

### Gaussian Process

::::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Priors

Choosing a prior for the GP length scale:

For an exponentiated-quadratic Gaussian process, the correlation
between two observations separated by distance $d$ is:

$$
\rho(d) = \exp\left[ -\frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{d}{\ell}\right)^2 \right],
$$

where $\ell$ is the GP length scale, called `lscale` in brms.

The length scale controls how quickly the fitted relationship can change:

- small lscale: rapid, local variation
- large lscale: broad, smooth variation

at a distance equal to `lscale`, the correlation is approximately 0.61.

When `gp(x, scale = TRUE)` is used, distances are expressed as
proportions of the observed range of `x`. Thus, a distance of 0.2
represents 20% of the observed predictor range.

Specifying an ecologically meaningful prior:

Rather than selecting inverse-gamma parameters directly, consider the
distance at which the GP correlation becomes weak. We define weak
correlation as:

$$
\rho_{\text{weak}}=0.1.
$$

The distance at which correlation reaches a specified value is:
$$
d_{\text{weak}} = \ell\sqrt{-2\log(\rho_{\text{weak}})}
$$

For $\rho_{\text{weak}}=0.1$, $d_{\text{weak}}\approx2.146\ell$,
or equivalently, $\ell\approx\frac{d_{\text{weak}}}{2.146}$.

Use `invgamma_from_weak_distance()` to specify a plausible range for $d_{\text{weak}}$. For example:

```{r}
#| label: default gp priors 1
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: false
invgamma_from_weak_distance(
  lower_distance = 0.20,
  upper_distance = 0.75,
  weak_correlation = 0.10,
  probability = 0.90
)
```

This expresses the prior belief:

There is 90% prior probability that GP correlation falls to 0.1 after a separation between 20% and 75% of the observed predictor range.

The function converts this statement into an appropriate inverse-gamma prior for lscale.
Meaning of the inputs

- lower_distance: smallest plausible distance at which correlation becomes weak, expressed as a proportion of the observed predictor range.

- upper_distance: largest plausible distance at which correlation becomes weak.
weak_correlation: the correlation considered ecologically negligible, commonly 0.1.

- probability: the prior probability assigned between the lower and upper distances, commonly 0.90.

As a general guide:

- smaller distances favour rapidly changing, local responses
- larger distances favour broad, smooth responses
- wider intervals represent greater prior uncertainty


```{r}
#| label: default gp priors 2
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
prior_info <- invgamma_from_weak_distance(
  lower_distance = 0.10,
  upper_distance = 0.5,
  weak_correlation = 0.10,
  probability = 0.90
)

prior_info
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
##### Default brms priors
```{r}
#| label: default gp priors
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
x <- wq_sub$dt_num
# Pairwise Euclidean distances
dx <- as.numeric(dist(x))
# gp(..., scale = TRUE) rescales distances so that
# the maximum distance is one
dx_scaled <- dx / max(dx)
dmin <- min(dx_scaled[dx_scaled > 0])
dmax <- max(dx_scaled)
# Ratio that the inverse-gamma quantiles must satisfy
target_ratio <- dmax / dmin
shape_equation <- function(shape) {
  qgamma(0.99, shape = shape, rate = 1) /
    qgamma(0.01, shape = shape, rate = 1) -
    target_ratio
}
alpha <- uniroot(
  shape_equation,
  interval = c(0.01, 1000)
)$root
alpha

beta <- dmin * qgamma(
  0.99,
  shape = alpha,
  rate = 1
)
beta
```

:::


```{r}
#| label: default gp priors old
#| results: markup
#| eval: false
#| echo: false
#| cache: true
# Inverse-gamma quantile function using the
# Stan/brms shape-scale parameterisation
qinvgamma <- function(p, shape, scale) {
  scale / qgamma(
    1 - p,
    shape = shape,
    rate = 1
  )
}


fit_invgamma_quantiles <- function(
                                   lower,
                                   upper,
                                   probability = 0.90
                                   ) {

  stopifnot(
    lower > 0,
    upper > lower,
    probability > 0,
    probability < 1
  )

  p_lower <- (1 - probability) / 2
  p_upper <- 1 - p_lower

  # Work on log(shape) and log(scale) so that
  # shape and scale are constrained to be positive.
  objective <- function(log_parameters) {

    shape <- exp(log_parameters[1])
    scale <- exp(log_parameters[2])

    fitted_quantiles <- qinvgamma(
      c(p_lower, p_upper),
      shape = shape,
      scale = scale
    )

    # Log differences give similar importance
    # to matching both the lower and upper limits.
    log(fitted_quantiles) -
      log(c(lower, upper))
  }

  fit <- optim(
    par = log(c(shape = 5, scale = lower * 5)),
    fn = function(par) {
      sum(objective(par)^2)
    },
    method = "BFGS"
  )

  shape <- exp(fit$par[1])
  scale <- exp(fit$par[2])

  fitted_interval <- qinvgamma(
    c(p_lower, 0.5, p_upper),
    shape = shape,
    scale = scale
  )

  list(
    shape = shape,
    scale = scale,
    probability = probability,
    lower_probability = p_lower,
    upper_probability = p_upper,
    lower = fitted_interval[1],
    median = fitted_interval[2],
    upper = fitted_interval[3],
    prior = sprintf(
      "inv_gamma(%.6f, %.6f)",
      shape,
      scale
    )
  )
}

invgamma_from_correlation_range <- function(
                                            lower_distance,
                                            upper_distance,
                                            target_correlation = 0.10,
                                            probability = 0.90
                                            ) {

  lower_lscale <-
    lower_distance /
    sqrt(-2 * log(target_correlation))

  upper_lscale <-
    upper_distance /
    sqrt(-2 * log(target_correlation))

  result <- fit_invgamma_quantiles(
    lower = lower_lscale,
    upper = upper_lscale,
    probability = probability
  )

  result$lower_correlation_distance <- lower_distance
  result$upper_correlation_distance <- upper_distance
  result$target_correlation <- target_correlation

  result
}
invgamma_from_correlation_range(
  lower_distance = 0.1,
  upper_distance = 0.4,
  target_correlation = 0.10,
  probability = 0.90
)
```

#### Fit model

```{r fitModel2ab, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ gp(dt_num), family = Gamma(link = "log"))
wq_sub |> summarise(
    median(log(NOx)), mad(log(NOx)),
    mad(log(NOx)) / mad(scale(dt_num))
)
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1), class = "Intercept") +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01), class = "shape") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_num") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class =  "sdgp")

wq_brm2b <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'only',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 thin = 5,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 backend = 'cmdstan',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 0)
```

```{r fitModel2bb, results='markdown', eval=FALSE, mhidden=TRUE, error=TRUE}
  scale_y_log10()
```

### Gaussian Process

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Fit model

```{r}
#| label: GP cyclic fit
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| mhidden: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 10
wq_sub <- wq_sub |>
    mutate(
      Mnth1 = cos(2 * pi * Mnth / 12),
      Mnth2 = sin(2 * pi * Mnth / 12)
    )
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ gp(dt_num) +
                gp(Mnth1, Mnth2),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"))
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1), class = "Intercept") +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01), class = "shape") +
  prior(inv_gamma(1.5, 0.06), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_num") +
  prior(inv_gamma(12.4, 5.7), class = "lscale", coef = "gpMnth1Mnth2") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sdgp")

wq_brm7a <- brm(wq_form,
  data = wq_sub,
  ## prior = priors,
  sample_prior = 'yes',
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 1000,
  chains = 3, cores =  3,
  thin = 5,
  backend = 'cmdstan',
  seed =  123,
  control =  list(adapt_delta =  0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
  refresh = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: GP cyclic conditional
#| results: markup
#| eval: true

    conditional_effects() |>
    plot(ask = FALSE, points = TRUE, plot = FALSE) |>
  wrap_plots()

wq_brm7a |> conditional_effects(effects = "dt_num") |>  plot(points=TRUE) |>
  _[[1]] +
  geom_point(data = wq_sub, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(y = NOx, x = dt_num, colour = Season))

newdata <- data.frame(Mnth = seq(1, 12, len = 100)) |>
    mutate(
        Mnth1 = cos(2 * pi * Mnth / 12),
        Mnth2 = sin(2 * pi * Mnth / 12)
    ) |>
  crossing(dt_num = c(2006, 2015, 2024))
# Expected response for every posterior draw
ep <- epred_draws(
  wq_brm7a,
  newdata = newdata,
  re_formula = NA
) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(Mnth, dt_num, .epred) |>
  group_by(Mnth, dt_num) |>
  summarise_draws(median, HDInterval::hdi)

ep |>
    ggplot(aes(y = median, x = Mnth)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_line() +
  annotate(geom = "point", x = wq_sub$Mnth, y = wq_sub$NOx) +
  facet_grid(~dt_num)
```

## Data preparation

```{r process3, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, fig.width=12, fig.height=12}

wq_sub2 <- wq |>
  group_by(Site) |>
  mutate(Min=min(dt_num)) |>
```

## Date model

### GAM

#### Fit model (priors only)

```{r additionalfitModel8a, results='markdown', eval=TRUE, mhidden=TRUE, cache=TRUE}
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ s(scale(dt_num)) + (1|reef.alias),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"))
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub2)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1),  class='Intercept') +
  prior(normal(0, 10), class='b') +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01),  class='shape') +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 10), class =  "sds") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class =  "sd")

wq_brm8 <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub2,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'only',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 thin = 5,
                 backend = 'cmdstanr',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta =  0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 0)
```


### Gaussian Process

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Fit model

**Warning** if exact GPs are to be computed, this models will take a
long time.  A faster version can be obtained by computing
Hilbert-space approximate GPs by indicating the number of basis
functions to be (e.g.) 20.

```{r}
#| label: GP date full fit
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| mhidden: true

  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)
wq_sub2 |> summarise(
    median(log(NOx), na.rm = TRUE), mad(log(NOx), na.rm = TRUE),
    mad(log(NOx)) / mad(scale(dt_num))
)
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub2)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1), class = "Intercept") +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01), class = "shape") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_num") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class =  "sdgp")

wq_brm10a <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub2,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'yes',
                 iter = 3000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 thin = 5,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 backend = 'cmdstan',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 0)
```

```{r}
  group_by(.draw) |>
  summarise(
    x = dt_num[which.max(.epred)],
    Nox = .epred[which.max(.epred)],
    .groups = "keep"
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  median_hdci(.width = 0.95) |>
  mutate(across(matches("^x"), lubridate::date_decimal)) |>
  mutate(across(matches("^x"), as.Date)) |>
  as.data.frame()
wq_peak
```

## Date and month model | Region

### GAM

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Fit model (priors only)

```{r}
#| label: date and month model RE Region fit priors
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ s(scale(dt_num), by = Region) +
                s(scale(Mnth), by = Region, bs = "cc") +
                (1|reef.alias),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"))
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub2)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1),  class='Intercept') +
  prior(normal(0, 10), class='b') +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01),  class='shape') +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 10), class =  "sds") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class =  "sd")

wq_brm13a <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub2,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'only',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 thin = 5,
                 backend = 'cmdstanr',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta =  0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 0)

```

```{r}
#| label: date and month model RE Region fit priors conditional
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
wq_brm13a |>
    conditional_effects(effects = "dt_num") |>
    plot(points = TRUE) |>
    _[[1]] +
    scale_y_log10() +
    geom_point(
        data = wq_sub2, inherit.aes = FALSE,
        aes(y = NOx, x = dt_num)
    )
```

#### Find the peak

```{r}
#| label: mixed date and month Region peak
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
newdata <- with(wq_sub2, data.frame(
  dt_num = seq(min(2010), max(2017), length = 1000),
  Mnth = 6
)) |>
  crossing(Region = unique(wq_sub2$Region))
wq_peak <-
    add_epred_draws(
        object = wq_brm13b, newdata = newdata,
        re_formula = NA,
        ndraws = 1000
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    group_by(Region, .draw) |>
  summarise(x = dt_num[which.max(.epred)],
    Nox = .epred[which.max(.epred)],
    .groups = "keep") |>
    ungroup() |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(x, Nox), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
    group_by(Region, variable) |>
  median_hdci(.width = 0.95) |>
  as.data.frame()
wq_peak
```

### Gaussian Process

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Fit model

```{r}
#| label: date and month model RE Region fit GP
#| results: markup
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
wq_sub2 <- wq_sub2 |>
  mutate(
    Mnth1 = cos(2 * pi * Mnth / 12),
    Mnth2 = sin(2 * pi * Mnth / 12)
  )
wq_form <- bf(NOx | cens(NOx_flag) ~ gp(dt_num, by = Region, k = 20, c = 5/4) +
                ## gp(Mnth1, Mnth2, by = Region, k = 20, c = 5/4) +
                gp(Mnth1, Mnth2, k = 20, c = 5/4) +
                (1|reef.alias),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"))
get_prior(wq_form, data = wq_sub2)
priors <- prior(normal(-3.1, 1), class = "Intercept") +
  prior(gamma(0.01, 0.01), class = "shape") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_numRegionBurdekin") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_numRegionMackayWhitsunday") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpdt_numRegionWetTropics") +
  prior(inv_gamma(4.6, 0.4), class = "lscale", coef = "gpMnth1Mnth2") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sdgp") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class =  "sd")

wq_brm14b <- brm(wq_form,
                 data = wq_sub2,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'yes',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 chains = 3, cores =  3,
                 thin = 5,
                 backend = 'cmdstanr',
                 seed =  123,
                 control =  list(adapt_delta =  0.99, max_treedepth = 20),
                 refresh = 100)

```

#### Conditional effects plot

```{r}
#| label: date and month model RE GP Region fit conditional

  _[[1]] +

newdata <- data.frame(Mnth = 6) |>

        Mnth1 = cos(2 * pi * Mnth / 12),

# Expected response for every posterior draw

) |>

  dplyr::select(Mnth, Region, dt_num, .epred) |>

  summarise_draws(median, HDInterval::hdi)

ep |>
  ggplot(aes(y = median, x = dt_num)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = wq_sub2, aes(y = NOx)) +
  ## annotate(geom = "point", x = wq_sub2$dt_num, y = wq_sub2$NOx) +
  facet_grid(~Region)
```
